required_facts.fact: In the climactic endgame of Mass Effect 3, as Reaper forces ravaged Earth and the Crucible—an ancient superweapon built by the Protheans—required activation at the Citadel, Commander Shepard and Admiral David Anderson led a massive galactic assault on London, England. The Reapers had constructed a towering conduit—a massive structure built from organic and metallic components—in the war-torn city. This conduit, built according to mass relay principles but modified by Reaper technology, served as a direct transport mechanism connecting the ground of Earth to the Citadel, which had been mysteriously repositioned above the planet. The conduit functioned unlike standard mass relays: it emitted a constant, brilliant beam of blue light into the sky, continuously transporting matter (primarily the dead and dismembered remains of slaughtered populations) directly from Earth's surface to the Citadel. The structure had no visible element zero core and, critically, allowed living organic matter to survive transit—arriving at ballistic but survivable speeds—rather than disintegrating as with conventional relays. The Reapers appeared to have multiple destination termini on the Citadel, as different individuals arrived at separate points on the station. The assault ran in two ground stages. First Shepard's shuttle landed to knock out a Reaper anti-aircraft "Hades Cannon" with M-920 Cain rounds so the Hammer ground force could land; the team then regrouped at a Forward Operating Base where Shepard held final words with surviving allies before Anderson gave the battle plan. The second stage pushed through occupied London to a missile battery, where Thanix missiles coordinated with EDI on the Normandy destroyed a Reaper Destroyer blocking the road to the conduit. Anderson then arrived by APC for the final charge. The galactic assault on the conduit was devastating. Allied forces from across the galaxy—humans, turians, asari, salarians, quarians, krogan, and others— launched a coordinated ground assault to penetrate the structure and secure access to the Citadel. However, Harbinger, the Reaper flagship and commander of the local Reaper forces, personally defended the conduit with overwhelming firepower, killing or maiming most of the allied assault force. The majority of the attacking soldiers were annihilated, their bodies adding to the biomass flowing through the conduit itself. Despite the horrific casualties, Commander Shepard and Admiral Anderson managed to fight their way through the structure and reached its heart. Anderson, wounded but resolute, helped push Shepard toward the conduit's exit point. Shepard survived the ascent through the conduit and materialized on the Citadel, while Anderson arrived at a slightly different point on the station. Upon reaching the Citadel, Shepard gained access to the Crucible's control mechanisms and the Catalyst—the artificial intelligence that had guided the Reaper cycle for countless eons. At this critical juncture, Shepard was confronted with a series of final choices that would determine the fate of the galaxy: to Destroy all synthetic life (eliminating the Reapers and the geth but also killing EDI), to Control the Reapers (uploading Shepard's consciousness to command them), to achieve Synthesis (merging organic and synthetic life), or to Refuse the Catalyst's offer (allowing the cycle to continue unchanged). The consequences of this choice—affecting the survival of the geth, EDI, the Reapers themselves, and organic civilization—would echo across the galaxy for generations.
Most of the galactic assault force on Earth is killed or maimed; the conduit's light beam carries thousands of casualties toward the Citadel.
Harbinger's personal defense of the conduit results in massive casualties among the allied ground forces.
Commander Shepard reaches the Citadel and gains access to the Crucible control mechanisms and the Catalyst.
Admiral David Anderson reaches the Citadel (severely wounded) and assists Shepard in reaching the Crucible.

Per the final choice (Destroy/Control/Synthesis/Refusal): - Destroy: All Reapers are destroyed along with the entire geth species and EDI; synthetic life is eradicated; the cycle of extinction theoretically ends. - Control: Shepard's consciousness is uploaded into and merges with the Reaper collective, giving Shepard godlike power but ultimately disembodying them; the Reapers are brought under Shepard's control. - Synthesis: Shepard's genetic code is merged with all organic and synthetic life in the galaxy, creating a new form of hybrid existence; the Reapers are transformed into custodians of this new synthesis. - Refusal: The Catalyst and Reapers are allowed to proceed with the cycle; the Crucible fails and the Reapers continue the harvest; galactic extinction continues indefinitely.
Shepard's ultimate fate is determined by the choice made and the Crucible's firing.

If Destroy or Control are chosen and sufficient War Assets are gathered, Shepard survives (though potentially as a Reaper in Control ending or as a hybrid in Synthesis); otherwise Shepard dies in the Crucible's activation.
Depending on the ending, Anderson either survives (on the Citadel) or dies from wounds sustained during the assault.
The galaxy's future is fundamentally altered: either the Reapers are destroyed (ending the cycle), controlled by Shepard, synthetically merged with organics, or allowed to continue their harvest.
If Destroy is chosen, the geth and EDI are killed along with the Reapers; if Control or Synthesis is chosen, they survive and are transformed.

Per the Extended Cut: epilogue scenes show Admiral Hackett ordering the fleets to evacuate Earth's orbit, the Normandy caught in the energy wave in transit and crash-landing on a garden world, the Charon Relay's core breaking up while the relay itself survives and the mass relay network is later repaired, and a Liara time-capsule message. A fourth outcome, Refusal (declining to activate the Crucible or shooting the Catalyst), dooms the current cycle to the Reaper harvest but leaves records that let a later cycle break the pattern, shown in an alternate Stargazer scene. Shepard's name is added to the Normandy memorial wall beside Anderson's unless a high-strength Destroy leaves Shepard's survival ambiguous.

evidence.text: If Shepard chooses to destroy the Reapers, the Crucible fires a red beam of energy that destroys the Reapers on and around Earth and transmits this energy to every relay the mass relay network through the Charon Relay before damaging the relays and the Citadel as well. If Shepard chooses to control the Reapers, the Crucible releases a blue wave of energy that brings the Reapers under Shepard's control, damages the relays, and leaves the Citadel intact. If Shepard chooses to merge organic and synthetic life, the Crucible fires a green beam of energy that causes the Reapers to cease attacking, but also damages the Citadel as it transmits the beam to the mass relay network. While Shepard chooses how to activate the Crucible, Admiral Hackett notices the Crucible activate and orders the fleet to disengage and rendezvous outside of the blast zone. Joker hesitates until the last possible second, desperate to save Shepard, before reluctantly following the fleet. However, he leaves too late. The Normandy jumps to FTL speeds but is caught by the energy released from the Crucible and crash\-lands in a jungle on an unidentified world.
evidence.for_key: Normandy crash-landing on a garden world after the Crucible fired

evidence.text:
2175 Aeia was the first planet of the Alpha Draconis System, in the Rosetta Nebula of the Milky Way. It was named after an asari scientist and lay on the list of forbidden mass relay destinations that led to uncharted space. Early information came from a single distant probe flyby, which reported two planets orbiting a white dwarf star. Closer scans by Commander Shepard's crew showed the planet sat within the star's habitable zone, held oceans of liquid water, and carried a thin nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere consistent with carbon-based plant life, raising the possibility that it was an unexplored garden world.

According to the Codex, humans first detected Aeia as an Earth-type world through telemetry in 2165. Probe surveys indicated lush vegetation, ample fresh water, and breathable air, prompting the Systems Alliance to upgrade the planet to a garden-world colonization priority. In 2173 the Alliance survey vessel Hugo Gernsback, under Captain Ronald Taylor, made planetfall on the jungle world. Ship transmissions stopped soon afterward. The precise fate of the command and crew was unknown, and they were presumed killed in action with their vessel destroyed.

The planet was the setting of the Mass Effect 2 loyalty mission Jacob: The Gift of Greatness, unlocked after Jacob Taylor was recruited. Its mineral deposits scanned as rich, with medium palladium, high platinum, medium iridium, and low element zero. By the time of Shepard's visit the planet showed four visible moons. The wiki noted a continuity conflict: the Codex named Ronald Taylor as the Gernsback's captain, but the mission established that he was second in command and became acting captain only after the actual captain, Harris Fairchild, died in the crash. The name may derive from Aiea near Pearl City, Honolulu, or from the Ancient Greek "aei," meaning "always" or "ever," a possible reference to the long delay between the crash and the activation of the distress beacon.

evidence.text: **Prerequisite:** Normandy Crash Site The Normandy's crash site is available automatically from the Cerberus Network as free DLC. When the DLC is installed, after acquiring the Normandy SR\-2, Shepard will receive an e\-mail from Admiral Hackett titled "Normandy Crash Site Located": From: Admiral Hackett Commander Shepard: Our scans in the Amada system have turned up something we thought you should see: the final location of the wreckage of the SSV Normandy. We thought this news might be important to you, but we also have an ulterior motive. The Alliance would like to honor the Normandy with a monument, to be built on the site of the ship's final resting place. We'd like to invite you to place the monument and be the first to walk on the site. There are still 20 crew members unaccounted for from the attack on the Normandy. If you find any signs of these lost crewmen, we ask that you report to the Alliance so that those heroes' families might find some closure. Godspeed to you, Commander. Travel to Alchera, Amada System, Omega Nebula, to start the assignment. These assignment notes are displayed after scanning the planet: *“Scans confirm the wreckage of SSV Normandy on the planet's surface. No life signs or mechanical activity detected. Stable landing zone located amid the crash site.”*

evidence.text: **Helyme** is a "post\-garden" world that once enjoyed an Earth\-like oxygen\-nitrogen atmosphere. It is still blessed with plentiful water, but a generally cold climate (and extreme seasonal shifts, courtesy of a 38\-degree axial tilt). Helyme is thought to be the homeworld of the arthenn, a spacefaring species which disappeared approximately 300,000 years ago. Precisely what happened to Helyme is still under debate. It appears a global extinction occurred, wiping out all native animal life forms more complex than zooplankton. Plant forms were not affected, but the lack of oxygen\-breathing life caused oxygenation of the atmosphere. Plant life was reduced after lightning storms ignited global wildfires. The leading theory for Helyme's devastation is an out\-of\-control biological weapon. For this reason, landing is strictly prohibited. The corporations of Illium have emplaced a network of quarantine satellites to dissuade would\-be looters from landing in the crumbling cities.

evidence.text: **Casbin** is a classic "pre\-garden" terrestrial world, with conditions similar to those on Earth millions of years ago. Its hot, humid atmosphere is mainly composed of nitrogen and carbon dioxide. An increasing amount of the surface is covered by simple lichen and algae. Should no unexpected calamity occur, these tiny plants will change the atmosphere to an Earth\-like nitrogen\-oxygen mix over the next few millennia. Due to its potential for future habitability and sapient life, Casbin has been designated a Sanctuary World by the Citadel Council. Landing is prohibited by law, and any disturbance of the fragile young ecosystem will result in harsh fines and imprisonment. At present, the planet is passing through the debris trail of a long\-period comet.

evidence.text:
Casbin was the second planet of the Hong System in the Armstrong Nebula, in the Milky Way. It was a classic "pre-garden" terrestrial world with conditions resembling Earth millions of years ago: a hot, humid atmosphere composed mainly of nitrogen and carbon dioxide, with a growing cover of simple lichen and algae expected to shift the atmosphere toward an Earth-like nitrogen-oxygen mix over the following millennia. Because of its potential for future habitability and sapient life, the Citadel Council designated Casbin a Sanctuary World; landing was prohibited by law, and disturbing the fragile ecosystem carried harsh fines and imprisonment. At the time it was passing through the debris trail of a long-period comet.

Despite the landing ban, Commander Shepard could visit Casbin during the assignment UNC: Geth Incursions, clearing a geth outpost and a geth encampment guarded by three geth heavy turrets. The encampment's array was transmitting regular encrypted data bursts over the Alliance's own FTL comm buoys to an unknown destination. Other points of interest included a salvageable crashed probe and a beacon for UNC: Locate Signs of Battle, beneath which was buried an identification tag belonging to Captain Thein, with no indication of who had hidden it or why. Enemies present included Geth Armatures, a Geth Dropship, and geth rocket, shock and sniper troopers. Surveyable minerals included gold, samarium and uranium, most of the sites lying in rough mountainous terrain, with the samarium deposit atop a sheer wall east of the Mako's landing zone.

The planet may have been named after a provincial capital of Iran, and its codex text may reference Earth's Proterozoic oxygenation. In Mass Effect Legendary Edition the lingering "Anomalous Signal" at the second point of interest could finally be switched off at a console, and the terrain gained 3D grass instead of plain green textures.

evidence.text: Shepard directs the Reapers to repair the mass relays and help rebuild the galaxy, also narrating this ending. - Depending on the player's Paragon/Renegade score, Shepard's narrative changes in regards to their utilization of the Reapers. In the **Synthesis** (green) ending, Shepard adds their energy to the Crucible's, thus creating a new, synthesized DNA. To choose this option, walk straight down the center path. The Catalyst explains that this is the best option, since synthesis is the pinnacle of evolution, and will render the Reapers obsolete. The Crucible emits a green light/beam, altering all denizens of the galaxy on the genetic level; the dividing lines between synthetic and organic life are blurred. The Reapers rebuild the damaged relays of their own accord, as well as share the collective knowledge of countless lost civilizations. EDI narrates this ending. Alternatively, Shepard can **refuse** to activate the Crucible. While speaking with the Catalyst, Shepard can reject deciding between the Destroy, Control, and Synthesis endings, insisting that a decision with such a massive impact on the galaxy and its people cannot be made, and that the war must end on Shepard's terms; or, Shepard can initially accept the Catalyst's options, but can then attempt to shoot the Catalyst instead. Both actions result in a Reaper victory and the continuation of the cycle of extinction. One of Liara's time capsules is then shown on an unknown world, and a recording of Liara explains that even though the people of her time failed in their struggle against the Reapers, those who find the capsule still have a chance to succeed. **Note:**  Choosing this ending will not unlock the Legend or Long Service Medal achievements. Additionally, reloading the final autosave before you make your galaxy\-changing choice removes the Catalyst NPC, *rendering you unable to shoot at it or choose the refusal ending in that state.* If you made a copy of the autosave where Shepard wakes up and meets the Catalyst for the first time and turned it into a regular save, you can let the entire scene play out normally; otherwise, the last manual save point is quite far behind. In the Destroy, Control, and Synthesis endings, the Crucible's blast causes the Normandy to crash land on an unknown planet. The survival of the Normandy's crew will rely largely on EMS: - If EMS is substantially low (below \~1750\) and the Destroy ending is chosen, nobody exits the Normandy. - If EMS is the same and Control is chosen or moderately high (above minimum, below maximum) and Destroy or Control is chosen, Joker and two of the player's most favored crewmates will exit a heavily damaged ship. - If EMS is 2800 or above and Destroy or Control is chosen, Joker and two of the player's most favored crewmates will exit a relatively undamaged ship. - If Synthesis is chosen, Joker, EDI, and the player's most favored crewmember will exit the ship; the former two will embrace. Various epilogue scenes will be shown, depicting the fates of noteworthy characters and races encountered throughout the journey. These scenes will depend on the choices made throughout the game, as well as the entire series. The surviving members of the Normandy's crew are then seen gathered near the memorial wall, honoring the memory of all those listed. The player's love interest (or Samantha Traynor if no love interest present: for example if Liara was killed by Harbinger's beam; likewise Miranda, Jack, and Kelly will not appear here even if they survive since they are not part of the crew) will place Commander Shepard's name plaque above Admiral Anderson's. If all crew members survived but Shepard does not have a current love interest, then the character Shepard interacted with the most will put the Commander's name on the wall. Afterwards, depending on EMS rating, the Normandy will be shown on the unknown planet, either being repaired or taking off into space. - If the Destroy option was chosen and the player has very high EMS, the plaque is shown, but not placed on the wall; instead, the crewmember holding the plaque only smiles, and a scene showing Shepard breathing in a pile of rubble is shown as the last scene before the credits roll. After the credits, a scene will be shown in which a Stargazer tells tales of "the Shepard" to a young child.
evidence.for_key: the Synthesis ending and Shepard's death

If she was Shepard's love interest, she will be shown looking at the stars instead of Miranda (Destroy and if Shepard is still alive). - Grunt and Wrex are welcomed back home to Tuchanka. If Grunt is dead, then a helmeted krogan will take his place next to Wrex. Grunt will not appear if Wrex is dead or if Synthesis was chosen. - Mordin Solus, Thane Krios, Legion, and any other squadmate (barring Zaeed, Kasumi, and Morinth) that wasn't saved in the course of Mass Effect 2 and Mass Effect 3 will be seen in individual shots, seemingly nodding their approval at Shepard's actions. If Eve did not survive, she too will be included in the montage. If fewer than six characters are dead, then the last image will be that of a charred Alliance helmet. - If Mordin Solus is still alive (which is only possible if Wreav is the Urdnot leader, Eve is dead, and Shepard convinced Mordin to leave the Shroud sabotage unfixed), Mordin will be shown near computer monitors studying a datapad in his hand while two krogan, one male and one female, are in glass tubes behind him (Control and Destroy). If Shepard does not have a love interest, Shepard's love interest is dead or does currently not serve aboard the Normandy (such as Kelly Chambers or Miranda Lawson, for example), then the character Shepard interacted with the most will put the Commander's name on the wall (with the exception of EDI, James Vega, and Javik). If that character is dead, then Liara T'Soni will be the one putting Shepard's name on the wall. If Liara is dead, then Samantha Traynor will take her place. - Exclusive to the Destroy ending, Shepard's love interest (or Liara, if Shepard does not have a love interest, the love interest is dead or is not a character who is currently aboard the Normandy) hesitates to put Shepard's name on the wall, and instead smiles hopefully. Shepard is later seen taking a single breath in a pile of rubble. - In the Synthesis ending, EDI and Shepard's love interest embrace after Shepard's name has been added to the wall. - Depending on how badly damaged the Normandy was, the final scene shows the Normandy either undergoing repairs or taking off from the unknown planet. Many years into the future, an old man known as the Stargazer tells the story of "The Shepard" to a young boy.

evidence.text: Now that both forms of life understand each other, the Reapers have stopped attacking the galaxy and begin to help rebuild of their own accord, and have also begun to share the collective knowledge of countless previous civilizations. EDI speculates that with the differences between organics and synthetics disappearing, mortality itself could one day be transcended to a new level of existence that she cannot imagine. Finally, she concludes by saying that no matter how far they advance, they will always remember Shepard and the others who died for this future. EDI's remarks on the new relationship between organics and synthetics differ based on the outcome of the geth\-quarian war. - If the geth destroyed the quarians, EDI states that synthetics are now free to choose their own paths. - If the quarians destroyed the geth, EDI states that organics no longer need to fear their synthetic creations. - If Shepard managed to achieve peace between the quarians and geth, EDI states that organics and synthetics can now coexist peacefully. The war against the Reapers is now over. Scenes on various worlds are shown, all based on Shepard's decisions during the last three years. Earth The aftermath depends on the outcome of the battle for Earth: - If Shepard failed to mobilize enough forces for the final fight and chose to destroy the Reapers, London will be seen in ruins, and a random Alliance soldier will be shown digging through rubble and finding a ruined Alliance helmet; no slideshows are shown. Otherwise, a restored London will be seen with a new conduit connecting it to the Citadel, which has also been restored. - If Shepard mobilized enough forces for the final fight, London will be seen damaged, but largely intact. - If Shepard chose to control the Reapers, a restored London will be seen being guarded and protected by the Reapers. - If Shepard chose Synthesis, then humans, aliens, and Reapers will be seen working together to rebuild Earth. Tuchanka The outcome on Tuchanka depends on the status of the genophage, who was leading the krogan, and Eve's survival: If the genophage was not cured: - A lone female krogan sits on a desolate Tuchanka. If Wrex was the Urdnot leader, another scene will show dead krogan lying amongst the rubble. - If Synthesis was chosen, it will cure the genophage instead. - If the rachni queen was saved (the real queen, not the breeder), the rachni settle on Tuchanka. If the genophage was cured: - If Eve survived, she can be seen holding a krogan child. - If Eve did not survive, another female krogan will take her place. - If Urdnot Wrex leads the krogan, scenes of krogan reconstruction are shown. - If Urdnot Wreav leads, scenes are shown of him amassing a krogan army. If Eve survived, she is shown having gathered her own army and confronting Wreav. - If Wreav leads, but Synthesis was chosen, his plans for retribution are seemingly abandoned and instead the krogan begin rebuilding their civilization. - If the genophage was cured and Synthesis was chosen, the ancient krogan temples are restored to their former glory. Rannoch The aftermath depends on the outcome of the battle for Rannoch: If peace between the quarians and geth was achieved: - In the Control ending, the quarians are shown having established a new city on Rannoch. A separate scene shows the geth building their own city, apparently with the aid of the Reapers. - In the Destroy ending, only the quarians appear. - In the Synthesis ending, the geth are shown to be working alongside quarians, who are now able to live without their environmental suits. If the quarians destroyed the geth: - If Synthesis was chosen, the quarians are still living in their environmental suits. If the geth destroyed the quarians: - If Destroy was chosen, Rannoch appears deserted. If the following people survived until the end, their fates are briefly shown - Miranda Lawson can be seen studying Reaper schematics with Oriana (Control), or planning construction with other technicians (Destroy or Synthesis). If Shepard's love interest, she will be seen looking at the stars (Destroy and if Shepard is alive). - Jacob Taylor can be seen working as an instructor (High EMS Control and Destroy), or comforting a female civilian with Brynn Cole (Synthesis or Low EMS Control and Destroy). - Samara can be seen visiting Falere at the new Ardat\-Yakshi monastery, or resuming her life as a Justicar if she failed to apprehend Morinth. - Zaeed Massani lounges on a chair by the coast (Destroy). - Kasumi Goto can be seen reuniting with Keiji Okuda (Synthesis, and if the Greybox was saved), or still holding the graybox in a room (Control and Destroy).

evidence.text: - While the Catalyst speaks, the voices of male and female Shepard can be heard echoing its dialogue. - Early in storyboarding, a "Reaper Queen" was used to confront Shepard instead of the Catalyst. The idea was that Shepard was so cybernetically enhanced they were able to plug directly into the Citadel and speak with the god\-queen on a virtual world. The queen viewed the Reapers' operations as unsustainable, and wanted things to evolve, but were incapable due to the limitations of their AI. The queen proposed things the other Reapers didn't like, so they sealed her away on the Citadel and never listened to her again. - Shepard's involvement meant a chance to force that evolution. The Renegade response would be to rudely refuse the offer, disconnect, and start blowing everything on sight. This would destroy the Citadel, Earth, and the Reapers, but give organics a chance. The Paragon response is broadly similar to the Control ending scenario, only Shepard becomes a "Reaper King" and still rudely calls out the queen. The Synthesis scenario is also largely the same, though it was an ending available to everyone. ##

evidence.text: **Note:** This section details Mass Effect 3's ending with Extended Cut installed. Extended Cut changes the presentation of the ending by incorporating additional cutscenes and dialogue choices and lowering the EMS requirements for certain outcomes. **Legendary Edition:**  Legendary Edition made several changes to the EMS thresholds for each ending. War Assets are no longer affected by any sort of Galactic Readiness system. Internally, they are treated as if the Galactic Readiness is permanently at 50%, but in\-game they are displayed as if Galactic Readiness is at 100%. The listings below show the value visible **in\-game**. Legendary Edition also includes Extended Cut and all other DLC for Mass Effect 3\. The Catalyst approaches Shepard and explains the purpose of the Reapers, itself, their origins, the Crucible, and the ways in which Shepard can utilize it to stop them; Destruction, Control, or Synthesis. The availability of choices and the severity of the collateral damage on the galaxy will be determined entirely by the player's Effective Military Strength. Note that the available endings are set immediately before Priority: Cerberus Headquarters; the remains of the Collector Base are added to the player's War Assets, but do not affect the final endings. **Warning:** If you are close to one of the choices and attempt to backtrack, a Critical Mission Failure message will pop up explaining the Crucible has been destroyed. - If EMS is between 0\-1599 (**LE:** 0\-3199\), only one option will be available depending on the player's choice at the end of *Mass Effect 2*: Control if Shepard saved the Collector Base or Destroy otherwise. Both will result in massive physical damage to Earth, with Destroy killing almost everyone on Earth. - If EMS is between 1600\-2349 (**LE:** 3200\-4199\), both Destroy or Control options are available, but either choice will cause some substantial damage to the galaxy. If the Collector Base was destroyed and Destroy is chosen, the damage to Earth will be somewhat less. - If EMS is between 2350\-2649 (**LE:** 4200\-5199\), if the Collector Base was saved, the Control option will cause no physical damage and the Destroy option will cause partial damage to Earth. If the Collector Base was destroyed, the Control option will cause substantial damage but the Destroy option will cause no physical damage. - If EMS is 2650\+ (**LE:** 5200\+) the Destroy and Control options will no longer cause any physical harm to the galaxy. - If EMS is 2800\+ (**LE:** 6200\+) the Synthesis ending becomes available. - If EMS is 3100\+ (**LE:** 7400\+) and the Destroy option is chosen, Shepard is seen barely alive, gasping for breath (if Anderson is shot by the Illusive Man, the player needs a higher EMS to see this short scene; in the Legendary Edition, Anderson's fate has no impact). The **Destroy** (red) option will result in the destruction of all synthetic life, including the geth and EDI as well as the Reapers. To choose this option, walk down the path to the right and shoot the power conduit in front of you. The Crucible will fire a beam/pulse into the mass relay network, spreading the blast across the galaxy but severely damaging every relay and the Citadel in the process. Some time later, the galaxy eventually finishes the repairs to the relays and recovers from the destruction the Reapers had caused. Admiral Hackett narrates this ending. - If EMS is substantially low, choosing Destroy will result in massive physical damage throughout the galaxy, as well as the annihilation of most life. Hackett's narrative is different in this ending; his outlook on the galaxy's future is shorter and far more bittersweet. The **Control** (blue) option results in Shepard sacrificing corporeality to command the Reaper fleet. To choose this option, walk down the path to the left and interact with the control terminal. The Reapers will then leave Earth at the will of the Commander. Instead of firing a beam, only a pulse will be released from the Citadel. The pulse spreads throughout the mass relay network, damaging them but leaving the Citadel intact. Shepard directs the Reapers to repair the mass relays and help rebuild the galaxy, also narrating this ending. - Depending on the player's Paragon/Renegade score, Shepard's narrative changes in regards to their utilization of the Reapers. In the **Synthesis** (green) ending, Shepard adds their energy to the Crucible's, thus creating a new, synthesized DNA. To choose this option, walk straight down the center path. The Catalyst explains that this is the best option, since synthesis is the pinnacle of evolution, and will render the Reapers obsolete. The Crucible emits a green light/beam, altering all denizens of the galaxy on the genetic level; the dividing lines between synthetic and organic life are blurred.

evidence.text:
The Stargazer was a humanoid entity of indeterminate species and background who narrated the deeds of "The Shepard" to a child companion in the closing scene of Mass Effect 3. Which of two Stargazers appeared depended on Commander Shepard's final choice in the battle for Earth.

If the Crucible was activated, a male Stargazer finished telling the tale, saying it happened long ago and that many details had been lost to time. If the Crucible was not activated and the Reapers continued their cycle, a female Stargazer of an unknown species finished the tale, explaining that her people knew of Shepard's actions and the war through archives left behind by Liara T'Soni; that information had saved the contemporary generation from the threat and was why they lived in peace. In either version the child asked to hear more, and the Stargazer replied that there was time for one more story.

According to trivia, the scene evolved from an early storyboarded Synthesis ending presented by a "Reaper Queen" featuring an asari mother and daughter. The male Stargazer was voiced by former astronaut Buzz Aldrin.
evidence.for_key: the Synthesis ending and Shepard's death

evidence.page: Tali'Zorah vas Normandy — Character Analysis (Part 5) — The Romance Arc and Conclusion
evidence.text: The essayist reasons: Tali would never choose Refuse (standing by while her fleet burns). Destroy is the least desirable for her because it would also wipe out the geth now helping rebuild Rannoch and risk the quarian liveships disabled in Earth orbit — but it is viable, especially if Shepard had already destroyed the geth on Rannoch. Control would eventually force her to keep putting down synthetic rebellions forever. Synthesis would appeal most to a Tali who lived to see quarian–geth peace. But factoring in Shepard's influence — whose goal was always to destroy the Reapers — the essayist concludes she picks Destroy, ending the Reaper threat "with a few shots from a carnifex."

evidence.text: As a result of Shepard's decisions, there are four outcomes to the story: - **The Alliance Fleet saves the Council (Paragon ending):** In gratitude for the sacrifices of the Alliance Fleet and Shepard's help, they offer humanity the chance to become a Council race. This ending is almost the same as the Renegade one, but the Council meets Shepard in the Presidium. Again, Shepard can nominate either Udina or Anderson to be the human representative, and they decide to unite all the Citadel races against the coming threat of the Reapers. - **The Alliance Fleet saves the Council (Renegade ending):** It is also possible to have a Renegade version of this ending. The ending is pretty much the same, but with the main difference being that the Council thanks Shepard within a dark room with background ominous music playing, and dialog being somewhat different. Whereas the Paragon ending has the Council praising Shepard's selflessness and heroism and stating that humanity is ready to join the Council, the Renegade ending has the Council impressed by Shepard's ruthlessness and determination to succeed, at first thinking that such indomitable will made humanity stubborn and even dangerous, but now realising that this is what makes them strong, thus making humanity a powerful ally. Possible by having a Renegade Shepard save the Council. - **The Council is destroyed (Paragon ending):** The Alliance forms a new Council, with a human chairman but the other races remaining on the Council. Shepard can nominate either Udina or Anderson to chair the new Council, and they prepare to combat the Reapers with the Alliance Fleet at the forefront. This occurs if Shepard does not save the Council, but is not a Renegade. - **The Council is destroyed (Renegade ending):** The Alliance forms a new Council, with no other races involved. Shepard can nominate either Ambassador Udina or Captain Anderson to chair the new Council, and they prepare to combat the Reapers with the Alliance Fleet at the forefront. If Shepard is a Renegade and claims humans should work with other races, Udina will remark that this is uncharacteristic of Shepard's previous actions, and goes on to form the human\-only council anyway. In all four endings Shepard leaves the Citadel aboard the Normandy, intending to find a way to stop the Reaper invasion. Series Navigation |  |  | Next → | | --- | --- | --- | |  |  | Storyline II |

evidence.text: **Note:** This section intentionally does not take into account changes made by the Extended Cut DLC or Mass Effect Legendary Edition (which incorporates all previous DLC including Extended Cut). See the following section for a breakdown of Mass Effect 3's ending with Extended Cut installed, or if you are playing Legendary Edition. The availability of choices and the severity of the collateral damage on the galaxy will be determined entirely by the player's Effective Military Strength. Note that the available endings are set immediately before Priority: Cerberus Headquarters; the remains of the Collector Base are added to the player's War Assets, but do not affect the final endings. **Warning:** If you take too long (two minutes) to make a decision, the Reapers will destroy the Crucible, an apt Critical Mission Failure message saying so. - If EMS is between 0\-1749 with either a save file imported from Mass Effect 2 or a new game started with Mass Effect: Genesis 2, only the Destroy or Control option will be available, determined by whether or not the Collector Base was destroyed or preserved. In any case, both options will result in massive physical damage to Earth, with Destroy killing everyone on Earth. - If EMS is between 1750\-2349, the choice between Destroy or Control options becomes available, but either choice will cause some substantial damage to the galaxy. - If EMS is between 2350\-2649, the Control option will cause no physical damage and the Destroy option will still massively damage the galaxy. - If EMS is 2650\+, the Destroy and Control options will no longer cause any physical harm to the galaxy. - If EMS is 2800\+, the Synthesis ending becomes available. - If EMS is 4000\+, and the Destroy option is chosen, Shepard is seen barely alive, gasping for breath (if Anderson is shot by the Illusive Man, the player needs 5000\+ EMS to see this short scene). The Destroy (red) option will result in the destruction of all synthetic life, including the geth and EDI as well as the Reapers. The Crucible will fire a beam/pulse into the mass relay network, spreading the blast across the galaxy but breaking apart every relay and the Citadel in the process. Joker and EDI will embrace. - If EMS is 4000\+, then three crew members will exit in the Destroy and Control endings; Joker and two of the player's most\-favored crew mates. evidence.text:
This page is a chronological plot synopsis of the Mass Effect 3-era fiction.

In Mass Effect: Retribution, the Illusive Man had Kai Leng abduct former operative Paul Grayson and infected him with Reaper nanotech; Grayson, turned into a Reaper puppet, was hunted across the galaxy and finally killed at Grissom Academy by David Anderson, Kahlee Sanders and the student Nick. Mass Effect: Inquisition followed C-Sec's Bailey investigating Executor Pallin's supposed corruption at Udina's direction. Mass Effect: Deception continued the Kai Leng, Gillian Grayson and Biotic Underground threads. Mass Effect: Conviction had James Vega brought aboard the Normandy SR-2 to guard the imprisoned Shepard after the Bahak incident. Mass Effect: Invasion recounted Cerberus general Oleg Petrovsky and Colonel Raymond Ashe using an engineered Adjutant crisis to seize Omega from Aria T'Loak, who surrendered the station rather than see it destroyed. Mass Effect: Infiltrator followed rogue Cerberus operative Randall Ezno turning against the Director's Reaper-tech experiments after they mutilated his handler Inali Renata. Homeworlds #4 followed Liara T'Soni, now the Shadow Broker, chasing Prothean leads to Thessia and Kahje.

The Mass Effect 3 recap covered the Reaper invasion of Earth and Anderson staying behind; the Mars Archives and the discovery of the Prothean device (Crucible), with the android Eva Coré and EDI; the war summit and the genophage cure arc on Sur'Kesh and Tuchanka (Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks, Urdnot Wrex or Wreav, Dalatrass Linron, Primarch Adrien Victus, and Eve); the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's exposure and death; the quarian-geth war over Rannoch, ending in the destruction of a Reaper and peace or genocide; the fall of Thessia and Kai Leng's theft of the Prothean VI data; the pursuit of Cerberus through Sanctuary (Henry, Miranda and Oriana Lawson) to Cronos Station and Leng's death; and the battle for Earth. The synopsis closed with the Illusive Man's death, Anderson's death, and the Catalyst offering Shepard the Destroy, Control, Synthesis or refusal endings, followed by extensive epilogue variations and the Stargazer framing scene.

evidence.text:
Mass Effect 3: Extended Cut was a free DLC pack for Mass Effect 3, released June 26, 2012 for all platforms (July 4 for PlayStation 3 in Europe) and built into the Wii U version. After many players complained the original ending was confusing and lacked closure, BioWare co-founder Ray Muzyka announced new content, and BioWare re-prioritized its post-release DLC schedule to make it. The pack added new cinematics and epilogue scenes expanding the original ending, varying by the player's choices and Effective Military Strength (EMS).

New cutscenes showed Shepard's squadmates being incinerated by Harbinger's beam or evacuated by the Normandy depending on EMS; Admiral Steven Hackett learning someone reached the beam; Shepard launched into the Citadel tunnel; the Crucible docking under attack at low EMS; a dead character replacing Joker in the final flashback, ending on the actual love interest; Hackett ordering the fleets to evacuate Earth's orbit, with a surviving squadmate convincing Joker to leave so the Normandy is caught in the energy wave in transit; two stranded soldiers on Earth affected differently by each ending; the Charon Relay's core breaking up while the relay survives and relays are later repaired (though low-EMS Destroy and Control still show relays exploding); species and crew aftermaths; and Shepard's name placed on the Normandy memorial wall beside Anderson's, left off in high-EMS Destroy to keep Shepard's fate ambiguous alongside the shot of Shepard breathing in the rubble.

Dialogue changes largely rewrote the Catalyst's lines, let Shepard investigate Reaper origins and the Crucible's abilities, and added a fourth option: refusing to activate the Crucible (via dialogue or by shooting the Catalyst), dooming the galaxy to another Reaper purge and triggering scenes of a Liara time capsule and an alternate post-credits Stargazer scene in which a later cycle achieves peace using the previous cycle's records. Fixes lowered the EMS needed for all endings from 4,000 to 3,100, restored ambient Normandy dialogue between Ken/Gabby and Garrus/Tali, and replaced the post-credits DLC advert with a thank-you message. EA later confirmed it would never charge for or remove the content.

evidence.text:
Kasumi Goto was described as the galaxy's most enigmatic thief, a master of stealth and infiltration with enemies everywhere but few who could put a name to her face. In Mass Effect: Foundation she was shown in an intimate relationship with her partner Keiji Okuda, who nicknamed her "Little Bird." She planned a heist against arms dealer Donovan Hock on Bekenstein; during it Hock stabbed Keiji in the head and stole his graybox, a neural implant storing memories and secrets. The dying Keiji begged Kasumi to survive and recover the graybox; she cloaked and left his body, vowing to make good on her word.

In Mass Effect 2, Cerberus tracked Kasumi down and she agreed to join Commander Shepard's mission against the Collectors on the condition that Shepard help her recover Keiji's graybox from Hock. Shepard met her on the Citadel's Zakera Ward using the password "Silence is golden." She settled in the Normandy's port observation deck among stolen effects. She rivaled Kelly Chambers for insight on the crew, being the only person to notice if Morinth replaced Samara, and displayed an unreciprocated crush on Jacob Taylor. Her loyalty mission, Kasumi: Stealing Memory, saw Shepard and Kasumi infiltrate Hock's gala, battle Eclipse mercenaries, and recover the graybox; one secret within could trigger galactic war.

In Mass Effect 3, six months after surviving the Suicide Mission, Kasumi resurfaced on the Citadel, feeding the salarian Spectre Jondum Bau a tip about indoctrinated hanar operatives aware of an Alliance black ops raid into batarian space. She secretly assisted Bau and Shepard tracking down the culprit, who was attempting to disable the hanar homeworld Kahje's defenses. Kasumi stopped the virus but the booby-trapped console exploded, seemingly killing her. If Shepard had recovered the graybox, she revealed the raid was Keiji's dangerous secret: the Alliance had raided batarians who found Reaper technology. She then revealed she had faked her death to escape Bau, and Shepard could convince her to aid the Crucible project by promising expensive equipment nobody would miss. If the graybox was never retrieved, she did not reveal herself or join the war. During the final battle she reported the Crucible ready. In the synthesis ending, if she kept Keiji's memories, she was seen holding hands with an apparition of Keiji; in destroy or control endings she held his graybox. In the Citadel DLC she plotted to rob the Silver Coast Casino and appeared at Shepard's party, constantly cloaking and decloaking in unexpected places.

evidence.text: Born on Palaven and a decorated engineer in Blackwatch, Macen Barro was touted by the Hierarchy to be a shining example of a turian citizen. There were concerns among Initiative leadership about whether or not he would leave his comfortable life behind to become the turian Pathfinder, but Macen was eager—so long as he could name his replacement: Avitus Rix, a former Spectre. Internal emails and screening interviews state Macen and Avitus met in the field and suggest that their relationship may be more than platonic. Macen Barro left the Milky Way aboard the turian ark Natanus in 2185\. #### Avitus Accepts Pathfinder Position Despite his initial hesitation, Avitus Rix complied with Macen's last request to take up the role of turian Pathfinder. A grief counselor was assigned to Avitus upon his arrival at the Nexus, but he has yet to show at a session.

evidence.section: Interface to take Meridian from the Archon
evidence.text: Fortunately, the final console is active already. Retrace Ryder's steps to the south and activate the console to end the battle. With his energy reserves cut off, the Archon is killed by feedback from his own wiring. Ryder is now able to bring Meridian online, and various worlds across Heleus blooming are displayed. (This doesn't actually change viability or activate any Vaults Ryder hasn't activated already, so all those missions are still available.) Ryder, the crew, and Ryder's twin emerge on the surface of Meridian, to be greeted by the rest of the Tempest crew and various allies. A victory speech, celebration, and the end credits follow. Congratulations, you have completed the main story arc of the game. If you had any side missions or Additional task pending, you will get a chance to get them done a little later. After the credits, a cutscene shows that the Primus escaped the battle. She's aboard her ship, orbiting Meridian, but departs. Epilogue: Home and Away begins immediately.

evidence.text: The kett flagship, Verakan, is a heavily armed warship that serves as the Archon's central command post for the kett incursion into the Heleus Cluster. Heavy main guns and exceptionally powerful kinetic barriers suggest that any frontal assault on the Verakan without a correspondingly powerful dreadnought would be suicide. The vessel appears to serve as a research center for studying newly captured Milky Way species. Both krogan and salarian captives were encountered aboard, indicating the Archon's interest in exalting new species and acquiring their genetic traits. The Verakan also houses many of the kett's most important Remnant relics, apparently gathered and presented to the Archon for study at his leisure. This fascination was evident in the Archon's private chamber, where he kept a special collection of Remnant technology and relics on display.

If Kate survived, news snippets will instead report that she was expected to read a thank\-you message to the Alliance soldiers who rescued her at an upcoming anniversary celebration of the thwarted terrorist attack on Terra Nova. She also sends the Commander the following message instead, titled "Glad you're okay." From: Kate Bowman Shepard, I called in some favors and found out how to get you and what you're working on. We've got a big celebration planned for the anniversary of you and the others saving Terra Nova. Last year we added a memorial for you, too. I guess that was premature, huh? I figure finding out who's attacking colonies is why you had to go undercover, so I won't invite you to come give a speech or anything. But I wanted you to know that all of us living on colonies are worried about what's happening in the Terminus Systems. And I'm really glad you're there to help. There's a lot of crazy military talk going around. I'm glad someone's there who's not going to take the easy way out. Thanks. Kate Bowman

evidence.text:
Avernus Station was a Cerberus research base constructed beyond the Omega 4 Relay after the events of Mass Effect 2, its primary purpose the study of Reaper technology. The events surrounding it were depicted in the comic Mass Effect: Invasion.

At some point a colony of Reaper creatures known as Adjutants broke loose aboard Avernus Station and overwhelmed the personnel. The Adjutants reached the transport ships docked at the station and crossed the Omega 4 Relay to arrive at Omega. Some Cerberus operatives survived the initial outbreak and fled to the station's exterior, hoping the high levels of cosmic radiation there would kill the Adjutants; this proved wrong, and the Adjutants followed them outside. The survivors were saved by the arrival of the Elbrus, a Cerberus warship commanded by General Oleg Petrovsky. Petrovsky and Aria T'Loak assisted the troopers in eliminating the remaining Adjutants and re-securing the station. The station was named after Lake Avernus, a volcanic crater lake in southern Italy that the ancient Romans believed to be an entrance to Hades.

evidence.text:
Admiral Daro'Xen vas Moreh was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board known for her clinical intellect and keen scientific interest in the geth, whom she regarded as machines built solely to serve their creators. She was said to have performed surgery on her childhood toys without guilt. She wished to return the geth to quarian control.

In Mass Effect 2, Xen was one of three admirals judging Tali'Zorah's treason trial, alongside Zaal'Koris vas Qwib Qwib and Han'Gerrel vas Neema. She viewed the trial as "a farce born of fear," called Zaal'Koris a coward and Han'Gerrel "an aging warship," and considered war with the geth foolish, though she had no qualms about experimenting on active geth. If Shepard brought Legion, she found it fascinating and mused about experimenting on it, prompting Legion to state it was not available and to call her control plans "unsound," a view Tali shared. Afterward she messaged Shepard that had Rael'Zorah's research been presented, humanity would have benefited; instead the quarians would reclaim their homeworld and the largest synthetic army in the galaxy.

In Mass Effect 3, Xen's research and development corps created white-noise jamming against geth ladar systems, prompting the Admiralty to vote for war, and she led the Special Projects group. If Tali was absent, Xen provided electronic support during the mission to disable a geth dreadnought, gave Shepard a prototype Arc Pistol, and later left in a geth fighter. She created the Sync Laser marking technology that cut through geth jamming, critical to the assault on the Reaper base on Rannoch. She repeatedly expressed interest in dissecting Legion or the Geth VI, argued with Tali over search-and-rescue versus salvage priorities, and briefed Shepard on the rescue of Admiral Koris. If she survived the geth-quarian war, she was sent to help build the Crucible, where Shala'Raan vas Tonbay described her as dissatisfied with the device but lending her technical skills. She was voiced by Claudia Black.

evidence.text:
Admiral Han'Gerrel vas Neema was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board and commander of the Heavy Fleet. He had a long history of provoking trouble along the turian border. A committed advocate of reclaiming the quarian homeworld, he argued that the Migrant Fleet had the largest fleet in the galaxy yet did nothing with it; Tali'Zorah countered that the ships might be needed against the Reapers, and he replied the quarians would need a homeworld to shelter non-combatants. Daro'Xen vas Moreh derisively called him "an aging warship," and he in turn dismissed Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib Qwib as a "whining suit-wetter."

Han'Gerrel was a friend of Tali's father, Rael'Zorah, having served with him aboard the gunship Yaska before their Pilgrimage. During a batarian raid that killed six of ten crew, the two, left alone on the bridge and under orders to hold position, disobeyed to recover a tramp freighter; they received medals and were sent on Pilgrimage early. During Tali's treason trial on the Migrant Fleet, Han'Gerrel sympathized with her and believed her innocent. He was the one person Shepard and Tali could confide in about the nature of Rael's experiments on the Alarei; despite his pro-war stance the experiments horrified him, and he vowed to keep the truth quiet to protect what Rael had wanted for the fleet.

Han'Gerrel was among the admirals who pushed for war against the geth, driving the synthetics to ally with the Reapers and trapping the Migrant Fleet within the Perseus Veil. When Shepard helped disable a geth dreadnought, Han'Gerrel ordered the fleet to press the attack on the geth flagship while Shepard's squad was still aboard. Back on the Normandy, Hackett and Shala'Raan condemned his recklessness, Raan threatening a treason charge. Shepard could hear his explanation or punch him and send him off the ship. He later clashed with Raan over comm about fleet maneuvering. After the Reaper controlling the geth was destroyed, Han'Gerrel ordered an all-out attack on the disabled geth fleet; whether he broke off depended on Shepard having earned the quarians' trust, and if not, the assault destroyed the entire Migrant Fleet.

evidence.text:
This page catalogs single-use equipment items used during Mass Effect 3 multiplayer matches, each lasting one mission and grouped into ammo, armor and weapon bonuses. Ammo bonuses added a separate "ammo damage" component to shots, heavily modified by the target's current defense type. They included Armor-Piercing Rounds (damage and penetration versus armor, no bonus to shields or barriers), Cryo Rounds (slows, weakens armor, can freeze unshielded enemies to prime Cryo Explosions), Disruptor Rounds (4x damage to shields and barriers, primes Tech Bursts), Drill Rounds (long-range penetration through cover; from Retaliation), Explosive Rounds (delayed detonation; from Retaliation), Incendiary Rounds (damage-over-time, primes Fire Explosions, stops enemy health regeneration), Phasic Rounds (10x versus shields and barriers; from Retaliation), and Warp Rounds (armor weakening, bonus biotic damage against Biotic Explosion-primed targets, 2x versus barriers).

Armor bonuses covered the Adrenaline Module (movement speed), Cyclonic Modulator (shield strength up to +150%), Power Amplifier Module (power damage), Power Efficiency Module (recharge speed), Shield Power Cells (shorter shield recharge delay), and Stabilization Module (weapon stability). Weapon bonuses were the per-class Rail Amps (assault rifle, pistol, shotgun, SMG, sniper rifle; +10/20/30% damage), the Strength Enhancer (melee damage), and Targeting VI (headshot damage). Several items became available in Store packs only after downloading the Resurgence Pack, and drill, explosive and phasic rounds only after the Retaliation Pack. Each item had three or four escalating levels.

evidence.text:
Ensign Jason Prangley was a biotic student at Jon Grissom Academy. He arrived at Grissom at age six, a shy child who barely spoke, and was known for constantly reading and studying battles, with some peers calling him a brownnoser. He proved capable of leadership when circumstances demanded it.

During the 2186 Reaper invasion, Cerberus attacked Grissom Academy to forcibly conscript its gifted students. If Jack survived the Suicide Mission, Prangley was among the students she protected; he was nearly killed by Atlas fire before his teacher intervened. When Commander Shepard arrived, Jason aided the firefight, providing biotic support strikes so that he and his teacher could retreat to higher ground. Afterward Jack derided his biotic fields as "weak," and he noticeably improved in later battles.

If Jack did not survive the Suicide Mission, Prangley interacted with Shepard in her place during the evacuation. Shepard found him stepping up to save Ensign Rodriguez from Atlas fire. Jason reported that their commanding officer had been killed, leaving him assuming command, and spoke on the students' behalf that they needed time to recharge after the strenuous exertion of biotics. In this scenario, Prangley later died protecting Rodriguez again from Cerberus troops just short of the hijacked escape shuttles. The survivors eulogized him aboard the shuttles, and Shepard invoked his memory to motivate the other students, either channeling their anger at his loss or holding up his sacrifice as an example to follow. Datapads left by Cerberus troops around the Academy indicate Prangley was specifically targeted as a prized acquisition.

evidence.text:
The Project Phoenix Vanguard was a playable multiplayer class in Mass Effect 3, one of the Project Phoenix operatives. Project Phoenix was a result of the Illusive Man's early experiments in enhanced human physiology, producing highly skilled combat and biotic specialists. After the Illusive Man adopted indoctrination to ensure his troops' loyalty, many Phoenix operatives defected to the Alliance to fight the Reapers. Their command of Cerberus lash and stasis technology, backed by strong biotic skills, made them valuable on the battlefield.

The Vanguard had 500 barrier and 500 health and used Biotic Charge, Lash, Smash and Fitness under Phoenix Training. Its regular melee was a shock baton, its heavy melee swung biotically charged lashes, and its grab dragged an enemy over cover for a charged biotic punch. Lash worked like a damaging, long-range Pull that could be evolved for shield and barrier penetration. The class could single-handedly create biotic explosions on armored enemies by pairing Smash with Biotic Charge, with Charge also restoring barriers for survivability. Smash produced a short-range, cover-piercing shockwave effect and, with its Biotic Combo evolution, left a priming effect on any target including large armored units, uniquely letting this Vanguard benefit from Warp Rounds' biotic damage bonus against hard targets like Atlases.

evidence.text:
The Human Vanguard was a cooperative multiplayer class in Mass Effect 3 (distinct from the Project Phoenix Vanguard and the Andromeda class of the same name). Its lore blurb repeated that humans joined the galactic community after discovering a Prothean data cache on Mars in 2148. Vanguards were feared frontline fighters who charged across the battlefield to surprise and destroy enemies in close combat.

The class had 500 barrier and 500 health and used the Alliance Training passive with the powers Biotic Charge, Shockwave, Nova and Fitness. Melee options included a punch sequence, a biotically-charged Biotic Strike heavy melee, and a Biotic Punch grab execution; it could combat-roll to dodge. It was the only class with Nova. Its signature tactic was the Charge-Nova cycle: Biotic Charge restored barriers and granted invulnerability during the animation, allowing a follow-up Nova, repeated continuously. Nova consumed barriers rather than triggering a cooldown; the Half Blast evolution halved its cost and damage for better survivability, and its Power Recharge evolution stacked to a 300% cooldown bonus. Shockwave was the only power usable safely at range to knock down enemies and detonate combos, and the only Vanguard priming power via the Lifting Shockwave evolution. The page details faction tactics: Charge-Nova was near-unstoppable against Cerberus (except Guardians and Atlases), highly effective against Collectors (but Seeker Swarms and Abominations were deadly), risky against Geth (Hunters, Primes and Rocket Troopers could stun), and effective against most Reaper troops, with extreme caution urged around Brutes, Ravagers and especially Banshees, whose glowing/teleport state must never be charged.
